newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal, Indonesia talks on Timor postponed.
newsitem.headline: Portugal, Indonesia talks on Timor postponed.

text.p: Talks between Portugal and Jakarta about the troubled Indonesian-occupied territory of East Timor, set for December 21 in New York, have been postponed, a foreign ministry spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

The delay was proposed by the United Nations, which is seeking to broker an accord over the territory, because of changes at the top of the international body where Ghanaian Kofi Annan will be formally appointed Secretary-General on Tuesday in place of Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
Lisbon, the former colonial ruler in Timor, readily agreed to the delay because "there were few prospects for any visible results" from the talks, the spokeswoman told Reuters.
Portugal and Indonesia have been meeting periodically under the auspices of the U.N. about the future of the territory which Jakarta invaded in 1975 and annexed a year later.

Human rights officials say that up to 200,000 people were killed in the military occupation and a subsequent crackdown and famine. The annexation was never recognised by the United Nations which continues to regard Portugal as the administering power.

Relations between Lisbon and Jakarta have sunk to new lows following the award two months ago of the 1996 Nobel Peace prize to Timor Roman Catholic bishop Carlos Belo and resistance spokesman Jose Ramos Horta.
The decision angered Jakarta which warned it could complicate the search for an accord with Lisbon.

The foreign ministry spokeswoman said that Portugal would propose that the next round of talks, for which a date has not been set, be preceded by preliminary meetings between the two countries' ambassadors to the United Nations.

Portugal backs the call of East Timor resistance movements for the people of the territory, located in the Timor Sea some 500 kms (300 miles) north of Australia, to be allowed to decide their own future.
But Jakarta says that a vote was taken back in 1976 and the territory opted to become part of Indonesia.
